reasons: Classification is correct: both clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows of ~180 days (Base § 4.0) and 12 months for 6-month renewal periods (Attachment § 2.0), well beyond the 60-day fallback and inside the rule's walk-away band (>90 days), so this is a genuine deviation rather than an acceptable fallback.

Redline reaches the preferred position on all material parameters: 30-day notice window, 12-month renewal term (including realigning the Attachment's 6-month periods), 60-day vendor reminder, and an uplift cap at the lesser of CPI and 3%; it also correctly fixes the Attachment's stray reference to terminating 'this Agreement'.

Party direction is right — MSL (vendor) gives the reminder to IBM (customer/our party) — and the failed minimal-edit checks (ratio ~0.70) are explained by the rule genuinely requiring insertion of the notice, reminder and cap mechanics into a short renewal sentence; no gratuitous rewriting is present.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day / 5% fallback.

Minor caveat worth noting to the deal team (not a defect): shortening the window symmetrically also lets the vendor exit on 30 days' notice, which in a manufacturing outsourcing deal reduces our supply-continuity protection; consider making the 30-day opt-out Customer-only while retaining a longer vendor notice.
